Every call is authenticated as the user's connection and reaches only what that connection's authorization allows, which the provider enforces on every request; the endpoints documented here are the ones this skill uses, and any other endpoint of this app needs the user to ask for it by name. Default to read and list calls, and confirm every write or new connection with the user. This file also documents the three constructs that turn a WhatsApp Business connection into automation, in the order they are used: the connection (the first step), a hosted function that runs a WhatsApp Business action through the Maton SDK, and a trigger that calls that function on a schedule or on an event. Running that automation includes administering it, and the skill covers that too: listing, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, searching, updating and deleting functions and their environment variables; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including pointing a destination at a URL the user supplies and rotating its signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying a trigger's past events, where a replay delivers that event again and re-runs whatever it starts; reading the account's request records, logs and metrics to debug a call, which is read-only; changing account settings, such as turning request and response body capture on or off; and watching events locally, including running a handler script the user supplies on each event with `--exec`. Every one of these that changes something is a write the user approves individually, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID. WhatsApp Business itself emits no Maton events: a schedule (`time`) or another connected app's event starts a WhatsApp Business function, and the files under `references/<source>/triggers.md` describe the sources Maton offers (time, Calendly, GitHub, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Slack, Stripe).

Use this skill when users want to interact with GitHub repositories, manage issues and PRs, search code, or automate workflows. For other third party apps, use the api-gateway skill (https://clawhub.ai/byungkyu/api-gateway). Calls run through the `maton` CLI with OAuth login, or over raw HTTP with a Maton API key where the CLI cannot be installed. Every call is authenticated as the user's connection and reaches only what that connection's authorization allows, which the provider enforces on every request; the endpoints documented here are the ones this skill uses, and any other endpoint of this app needs the user to ask for it by name. Default to read and list calls, and confirm every write or new connection with the user. This file also documents the three constructs that turn a GitHub connection into automation, in the order they are used: the connection (the first step), a hosted function that runs a GitHub action through the Maton SDK, and a trigger that calls that function on a schedule or on an event. Running that automation includes administering it, and the skill covers that too: listing, reauthorizing and deleting connections, and changing or clearing a connection's access policy, which sets the endpoints it may call; creating, deploying, searching, updating and deleting functions and their environment variables; creating, updating and deleting triggers and their destinations, including pointing a destination at a URL the user supplies and rotating its signing secret; listing, inspecting and replaying a trigger's past events, where a replay delivers that event again and re-runs whatever it starts; reading the account's request records, logs and metrics to debug a call, which is read-only; querying Maton's context graph, the IDs and relations of GitHub objects the gateway has seen, and adding or removing tags and metadata on those records in Maton; changing account settings, such as turning request and response body capture or context capture on or off; and watching events locally, including running a handler script the user supplies on each event with `--exec`. Every one of these that changes something is a write the user approves individually, and deletions and secret rotations are confirmed by exact ID. GitHub is itself a Maton event source, with its own events in `references/github/triggers.md`; a schedule (`time`) or another connected app's event starts a GitHub function as well, and the files under `references/<source>/triggers.md` describe the sources Maton offers (time, Calendly, GitHub, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, Slack, Stripe).

latestVersion.changelog:
Complete rewrite of the execution model and update to Notion API 2025-09-03.

Breaking
- Removed the notion-cli dependency. All operations are now plain curl calls
  against the official API. The previous version documented a CLI that was
  never distributed, so its commands could not run as written.

Changed
- Pinned to Notion-Version 2025-09-03. Databases are now addressed as data
  sources; added guidance on the database_id vs data_source_id split, which is
  the most common source of 404s after the upgrade.
- Token format updated to ntn_ (secret_ still supported).
- Profiles now have a concrete mechanism: ~/.config/notion/<profile>.key, with
  an explicit NOTION_API_KEY taking precedence over NOTION_PROFILE.
- Safety rules moved to the top of the skill as five operating rules applied
  before any request.
- Schema-change flow tightened: fetch current schema, diff, present to the
  user, apply only what was confirmed. Additive changes preferred over
  in-place property retyping, which discards incompatible values.

Added
- Pagination handling (has_more / next_cursor) with a rule against summarizing
  a database from a single unpaginated response.
- Error reference table covering validation_error, restricted_resource,
  object_not_found, conflict_error, and rate_limited, with what each usually
  means in practice.
- Notes that GET /pages/{id} does not return body content, that nested blocks
  require separate calls, that formula and rollup properties are read-only,
  and that view filters are UI-only.
- Property format reference including status, people, and phone_number.
